title: Daily Devotional #15
paragraphs: As I read Matthew chapter 15 today, I was struck by how the religious leaders of the time were so focused on the external practices of religion, while neglecting the true heart of it. Jesus rebuked them for their hypocrisy and reminded them that it's not what goes into the mouth that defiles a person, but what comes out of it.

This reminds me of how easy it is to get caught up in the outward expressions of faith, without truly examining our hearts and motives. We can go through the motions of prayer, attending church, and reading the Bible, but if our hearts aren't in the right place, it's all for nothing.

Lord, I pray that you would help me to truly seek you with my whole heart, and not just go through the motions of religious practice. Help me to examine my heart and motives, and to repent of anything that is not pleasing to you.

I also want to take note of the faith of the Canaanite woman who came to Jesus pleading for her daughter's healing. Despite being told by the disciples to go away, and even being called a dog by Jesus himself, she persisted in her faith and humility. She recognized Jesus as the Son of David and begged for his mercy. And because of her faith, her daughter was healed.

Lord, I want to have the kind of faith that the Canaanite woman had. Help me to persist in my prayers and to trust in your mercy and grace, even when the answer seems delayed or the situation seems impossible. Help me to recognize you as the Son of God, and to trust in your power to heal and restore.
Thank you for your word, Lord, and for the lessons it teaches us about true faith and the condition of our hearts. May we always seek you with all our heart, soul, and mind.
